Zillow pack from the desk series file. Latest print in file: FY2026Q2 (period end 2026-06-30).

Zillow gets paid by people who want to meet a house shopper. Agents pay for the For Sale line, the advertising on homes that are listed for sale. Zillow Home Loans is the mortgage line, earned when the company funds a loan. Landlords and property managers pay for the Rentals line. Those are the revenue lines the charts print.

For Sale is the engine. It is the large line. Rentals is the line that is still compounding. The company used to buy houses itself. That book is gone. It still shows up as a spike on the quarterly revenue chart, and it is not the For Sale line.

What is compounding now is Rentals. What is mature is For Sale. Look at the For Sale versus Rentals chart. The annual revenue chart is the long view, with one caution under it: 2018 and 2019 still include the houses the company bought and sold, and from 2020 the annual revenue line leaves those out, because that is how the later reports present the business.

Risks

  • The business breaks if shoppers stop starting here and agents stop paying to meet them. The trips to watch are visits, which means how many times people open the site and the apps; average monthly unique users, which means how many different people show up in a typical month; and the audience share the company quotes.
  • The mortgage line moves with rates and with how many loans Zillow Home Loans actually funds.
  • Another portal can take the agent dollar. That shows up on the For Sale line.
  • Rentals stops compounding, or the listings the site depends on get pulled.

Close competitors

  • Redfin — a brokerage with its own site, so it both sends shoppers and competes for the agent.
  • Homes.com (CoStar) — a portal built to sell agents the same kind of advertising.
  • Realtor.com — the other large listings site shoppers already know.
  • Compass — a brokerage that can keep its agents off a portal.
  • Opendoor — buys houses, which is the model Zillow left.

Unit economics, data access, and how the company is run are written up separately, and this page does not repeat them.
